strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): working line while Hermes reads the files of a folder. {folder} is the folder name, {done} the files read so far, {total} all files. Animated dots follow.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says this when a folder it should read does not exist (deleted, or its drive was ejected). {path} is the folder path. Buttons follow.
strings.en: {path} isn't reachable right now. Is the drive still connected?
strings.de: {path} ist gerade nicht erreichbar. Ist das Laufwerk noch da?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' first message when the chat opens. Folder buttons follow.
strings.en: Hi! I'm Hermes and I tidy up your documents. Where are they now?
strings.de: Hallo! Ich bin Hermes und räume deine Dokumente auf. Wo liegen sie bisher?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Button in the chat that opens the system folder picker.
Hermes chat (F2): The user typed or picked a folder that is not one of the known filing folders; Hermes asks before reading it. {name} is the name of the folder; its path follows in small type below.
strings.en: “{name}” isn't a folder I know. Read it anyway?
strings.de: „{name}“ ist kein Ordner, den ich kenne. Trotzdem lesen?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes found the folder the user typed and asks whether it is the right one. {name} is the name of the folder; its path follows in small type below.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks which folder the user means when the name they said fits several existing folders. The full paths follow as buttons. {name} is the name as the user said it.
strings.en: Which folder do you mean by “{name}”?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes cannot store a rule it made, because the check the rule form runs refuses it. Nothing was stored. {reason} is one of the short reasons that follow.
strings.de: Diese Regel kann ich nicht speichern: {reason}

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: the rule has no condition that recognises documents.
strings.en: It has nothing to recognise documents by.
strings.de: Es fehlt, woran ich die Dokumente erkenne.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: a condition of the rule, such as the sender, has no text.
strings.de: Bei einer Bedingung fehlt der Wert.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: a regular expression of the rule does not work. {reason} is the one-line reason of the regex library, in English.
Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: the IBAN of a condition fails its checksum.
Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: the rule has no place to file documents to.
Hermes chat (F2): Reason in the refused-rule sentence: the place to file to contains something Hermes cannot use.
strings.en: The target folder can't be used.
strings.de: Der Zielordner lässt sich nicht verwenden.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Button answering the question about an unknown folder: read it anyway.
Hermes chat (F2): Button in the chat that drops the current plan or question. Nothing is changed.
Hermes chat (F2): The user typed an answer, and Hermes asks them to confirm the option it understood by tapping it. {choice} is the label of that option.

Hermes chat (F2): A folder the user typed, picked or named does not exist or is not a folder. {name} is the name of the folder as the user gave it. Buttons to pick another folder or to try again follow.
strings.en: I can't find the folder “{name}”. Maybe the drive isn't connected.
strings.de: Den Ordner „{name}“ finde ich nicht. Vielleicht ist der Datenträger nicht angeschlossen.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' report after reading a folder that has several areas (top-level folders with their own order). {count} is the number of files, {areas} the number of areas, for example '3 areas'. A list of areas follows.
strings.en: Done reading: {count} files in {areas} areas. This is the order I see:
strings.de: Hab ich gelesen: {count} Dateien in {areas} Bereichen. Die Ordnung sieht so aus:

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' report after reading a folder that has exactly one area (a top-level folder with its own order). {count} is the number of files.
strings.en: Done reading: {count} files in one area. This is the order I see:
strings.de: Hab ich gelesen: {count} Dateien in einem Bereich. Die Ordnung sieht so aus:

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' report after reading a folder in which it sees no fixed order. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {count} is the number of files.
strings.en: Done reading: **{count} files**. I don't see a fixed order in them yet.
strings.de: Hab ich gelesen: **{count} Dateien**. Eine feste Ordnung erkenne ich darin noch nicht.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says this when a folder holds no files it can read. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: {folder} has no files I can read.
strings.de: In {folder} liegen keine Dateien, die ich lesen kann.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says this when reading a folder failed. {reason} is the system's error text.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says this when a folder holds too many files to read. {folder} is the folder name, {limit} the largest number of files it reads.
strings.en: {folder} is too big for me: more than {limit} files. Pick a subfolder.
strings.de: {folder} ist mir zu groß: mehr als {limit} Dateien. Nimm einen Unterordner.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Describes an area whose files lie directly in it, with no subfolders, in the list of areas.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('year'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('month'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('date'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('number'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('sender'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('kind'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('bank'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('insurer'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('vehicle'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('child'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('property'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.
Hermes chat (F2): Singular, lower case: what a folder level of an area stands for ('subfolder'), used in the description of an area such as 'by year, then sender'.

Hermes chat (F2): Row under the areas of a folder when more areas exist than are listed: how many more areas there are and the names of the next few, cut off by the dots. The number of files in them is added after the row. {names} is a comma separated list, {count} a number.
Hermes chat (F2): Dim row under the list of areas: folders without a recognisable order. {names} is a comma separated list of folder names.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' question after the list of areas: whether new files shall be filed in the same way.
strings.en: Shall I sort new files in the same way?
strings.de: Soll ich neue Dateien genauso einsortieren?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button to the question whether new files shall be filed the same way (primary choice).
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button under the list of areas: show every area, not only the first ones. {areas} is the number of areas.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes confirms the folder where new files are filed. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: Good. I'll file new files in {folder} like that.
strings.de: Gut. Neue Dateien lege ich in {folder} so ab.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes offers to move duplicate files to the trash. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {names} is a comma separated list of folder names, {count} the number of duplicates.
strings.en: **{count} files** in {names} are duplicates; the original is already in your order. They can go. Move them to the trash?
strings.de: In {names} liegen **{count} Dateien doppelt**, das Original liegt schon in deiner Ordnung. Die können weg. In den Papierkorb?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: move the files to the trash.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: leave the files where they are.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports files moved to the trash. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {count} is the number of files. The quoted phrase is what the user can type to undo.
strings.en: Done: **{count} files** are in the trash. “Undo that” brings them back.
strings.de: Erledigt: **{count} Dateien** liegen im Papierkorb. „Mach das rückgängig“ holt sie zurück.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Added to the trash report when some files were left alone. {skipped} is a number.
strings.de: {skipped} habe ich gelassen, weil sie sich geändert haben.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes confirms it leaves the duplicate files where they are.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks which folder new files arrive in. Folder buttons follow.
strings.de: Wo kommt Neues bei dir an?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: the user does not want to answer now.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' reply to 'Later'.
strings.en: Fine. Write to me when you need something.
strings.de: Gut. Schreib mir, wenn du etwas brauchst.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks which folder to tidy up. Folder buttons follow.
strings.en: Which folder shall I tidy up?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks which folder to read to learn its order. Folder buttons follow.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes refuses to tidy a folder into itself. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: {folder} is where you file your documents. I won't tidy it into itself.
strings.de: In {folder} legst du deine Dokumente ab. Den räume ich nicht in sich selbst auf.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes' report after reading the folder to tidy up. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {folder} is the folder name, {count} the number of files. Target folder buttons follow.
strings.en: Sure! **{count} files** are in {folder}. Where should they go?
strings.de: Gern! In {folder} liegen **{count} Dateien**. Wohin damit?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes does not know yet where the user files documents. Folder buttons follow.
strings.en: I don't know a folder for your documents yet. Where are they now?
strings.de: Ich kenne noch keinen Ordner für deine Dokumente. Wo liegen sie bisher?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks whether to tidy a folder only now or on every new file. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: Shall I tidy up “{folder}” just now, or from now on whenever something arrives?
strings.de: Soll ich „{folder}“ nur jetzt aufräumen oder ab sofort immer, sobald etwas reinkommt?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: tidy up only this one time.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: tidy up every new file in the folder from now on, as soon as something arrives.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks whether to copy or to move the files. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {folder} is the folder the files come from.
strings.de: **Kopieren** (Originale bleiben liegen) oder **verschieben** (sie ziehen aus {folder} aus)?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: copy the files; the originals stay.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button: move the files out of the source folder.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes confirms that the plan was dropped and nothing was changed.
strings.en: Fine, I'll leave everything as it is.
strings.de: Gut, ich lasse alles, wie es ist.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports a finished filing run. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {done} is the number of files filed, {stays} the number that stay, {folder} the source folder name.

Hermes chat (F2): added to the report of a filing run when files that already lay in an archive folder were renamed or moved as well, because the folder levels changed. {count} is the number of those files, {folder} the name of the archive folder they lie in.
strings.en: {count} files already in {folder} were renamed or moved.
strings.de: {count} Dateien, die schon in {folder} lagen, wurden umbenannt oder verschoben.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): added to the error message when a tidy-up over several archive folders stopped part-way. {count} is the number of files in the remaining archive folders that were not renamed or moved.
strings.en: {count} files in other archive folders were not renamed or moved.
strings.de: {count} Dateien in anderen Archivordnern wurden nicht umbenannt oder verschoben.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Added to the filing report when some files were skipped. {skipped} is a number.
strings.en: I skipped {skipped} because they changed in the meantime.
strings.de: {skipped} habe ich übersprungen, weil sie sich inzwischen geändert haben.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it hands the tidy-up over to the "Filing" tab (German: "Ablegen") once the source and the target folder are known. The tab name must match the tab title.
strings.en: I'm planning this in the "Filing" tab. There you see live what goes where, and you file it with one click.
strings.de: Ich plane das im Tab „Ablegen“. Dort siehst du live, was wohin kommt, und legst mit einem Klick ab.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports a run that was done in the "Filing" tab and copied the files. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {filed} is the number of files copied, {left} the number that are left, {folder} the source folder name.
strings.en: Done: **{filed} files** copied. {left} are still in {folder}.
strings.de: Fertig: **{filed} Dateien** kopiert. {left} liegen noch in {folder}.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports a run that was done in the "Filing" tab and moved the files. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {filed} is the number of files moved, {left} the number that are left, {folder} the source folder name.
strings.en: Done: **{filed} files** moved. {left} are still in {folder}.
strings.de: Fertig: **{filed} Dateien** verschoben. {left} liegen noch in {folder}.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes offers to move files to the trash that already exist in the archive with the same content. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {count} is a number, {folder} the source folder, {target} the archive folder.
strings.en: **{count} files** from {folder} are already in {target} (same content). They can go. Move them to the trash?
strings.de: **{count} Dateien** aus {folder} liegen schon in {target} (gleicher Inhalt). Die können weg. In den Papierkorb?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Name of a run in the undo history for files Hermes filed by itself, without being asked in the chat. {folder} is the name of the folder the files went into.
Hermes chat (F2): Name of a filing run in the undo history. {folder} is the source folder name.
Hermes (filing continuously): Name of the run in the undo history that Hermes made by itself for new files of a read folder. {folder} is the read folder name.
Hermes chat (F2): Name of a trash run in the undo history. {folder} is the folder name.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button that undoes the last run of Hermes.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says there is no run to undo.
strings.en: There's no run I can undo.
strings.de: Es gibt keinen Lauf, den ich rückgängig machen kann.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks to confirm the undo of a run that moved files. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {name} is the run name, {count} the number of files, {when} the time, {folder} the folder the files return to.
strings.en: The last run “{name}” filed **{count} files** ({when}). All {count} go back to {folder}.
strings.de: Der letzte Lauf „{name}“ hat **{count} Dateien** abgelegt ({when}). Alle {count} gehen zurück nach {folder}.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks to confirm the undo of a run that copied files. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {name} is the run name, {count} the number of files, {when} the time.
strings.en: The last run “{name}” copied **{count} files** ({when}). I'll take the copies out again; the originals stay.
strings.de: Der letzte Lauf „{name}“ hat **{count} Dateien** kopiert ({when}). Ich nehme die Kopien wieder heraus, die Originale bleiben.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks to confirm the undo of a run that moved files to the trash. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {name} is the run name, {count} the number of files, {when} the time.
strings.en: The last run “{name}” put **{count} files** in the trash ({when}). All {count} come back.
strings.de: Der letzte Lauf „{name}“ hat **{count} Dateien** in den Papierkorb gelegt ({when}). Alle {count} kommen zurück.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Primary answer button to the undo question.
Hermes chat (F2): Time of a run when it was today. {time} is a clock time.
Hermes chat (F2): Time of a run when it was before today. {date} is a date, {time} a clock time.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports a finished undo. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {count} is the number of files.
Hermes chat (F2): Added to the undo report when some files stayed. {left} is a number.
strings.en: I left {left} because they changed or their old place is taken.
strings.de: {left} habe ich gelassen, weil sie sich geändert haben oder ihr alter Platz belegt ist.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says in its opening bubble that one document waits for the user's decision, because no rule could place it.
strings.en: One document is waiting for you.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says in its opening bubble that several documents wait for the user's decision, because no rule could place them. {count} is a number of two or more.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button under the note about waiting documents; starts going through them one question at a time.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks about a group of waiting documents that all belong in the same folder. {count} is the number of documents, {folder} the folder they would go to, {names} the first file names, separated by commas.
strings.en: {count} of them belong in “{folder}”: {names}. Shall I file them there?
strings.de: {count} davon gehören nach „{folder}“: {names}. Soll ich sie dort einordnen?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Primary answer button to the question about a group of waiting documents; files them in the folder named in the question.
Hermes chat (F2): Primary answer button to the question about one unsure waiting document; files it in the folder where similar documents lie. {folder} is that folder.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button to the question about waiting documents; leaves them as they are for now.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it cannot tell where one waiting document belongs. {name} is the file name.
strings.de: Bei „{name}“ bin ich nicht sicher, wohin es gehört.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Added to the note about an unsure waiting document: similar documents already lie in this folder. {folder} is the folder.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it cannot tell where a group of waiting documents belongs; they have the same sender or would go to the same folder. {count} is the number of documents, two or more, {names} the first file names, separated by commas.
strings.en: I'm not sure where these {count} belong: {names}.
strings.de: Bei diesen {count} bin ich nicht sicher, wohin sie gehören: {names}.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Primary answer button to the question about a group of unsure waiting documents; files all of them in the folder where similar documents lie. {folder} is that folder.
Hermes chat (F2): Line shown while Hermes files waiting documents.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes ends the walk through the waiting documents. **Double asterisks** mark bold text and must stay around the same words. {filed} is the number of documents filed, {left} the number still waiting.
strings.en: That was all. **{filed}** filed, {left} still waiting.
strings.de: Das waren alle. **{filed}** eingeordnet, {left} warten weiter.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says no document waits for the user any more.
strings.en: No document is waiting for you any more.
strings.de: Es wartet kein Dokument mehr auf dich.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes reports that some waiting documents could not be filed. {count} is the number, {reason} the first technical reason.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it cannot search inside the chat yet and offers to open the search.
strings.en: I can't search in the chat yet. I'm happy to open the search for you.
strings.de: Im Chat suchen kann ich noch nicht. Die Suche öffne ich dir gern.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Button in the chat that opens the document search.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it cannot explain yet why a file is where it is. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: I can't explain yet why something is where it is. What would you like to do?
strings.de: Erklären, warum etwas wo liegt, kann ich noch nicht. Was hast du vor?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it cannot move a set of files described in words yet. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: I can't move a set of files like that yet. What would you like to do?
strings.de: Mehrere Dateien auf einmal verschieben kann ich so noch nicht. Was hast du vor?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it did not understand the text. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: I did not get that. What would you like to do?
strings.de: Das habe ich nicht verstanden. Was möchtest du tun?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Button offering the search when Hermes did not understand.
Hermes chat (F2): Button offering to tidy up a folder when Hermes did not understand.
Hermes chat (F2): Button offering to read the order of the archive when Hermes did not understand.
Hermes chat (F2): Button offering to undo the last run when Hermes did not understand.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes explains it needs its local language model to understand typed sentences and offers to download it. {size} is the download size, for example '2741 MB'. A button to download follows.
strings.en: To understand sentences I need my language model ({size}, one time, stays on this computer). Shall I download it?
strings.de: Um Sätze zu verstehen, brauche ich mein Sprachmodell ({size}, einmalig, bleibt auf diesem Rechner). Soll ich es laden?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Primary button that starts the download of the language model.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says the Hermes switch of the Hermes page in the settings is off, so it cannot understand typed sentences, and offers to switch it on. A button to switch it on follows.
strings.en: My AI is switched off, so I can't understand sentences. Shall I switch it on?
strings.de: Meine KI ist ausgeschaltet, so verstehe ich keine Sätze. Soll ich sie einschalten?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says its language model finished downloading and can be used now. Shown before it answers the sentence that waited for the model, or before the first question.

Hermes chat (F2): An entry in the list of folders without a fixed order. It stands for the files that lie directly in the folder Hermes read, not in a subfolder. {folder} is the name of that folder as the chat shows it, for example 'Downloads'.
Hermes chat (F2): Primary button that switches the AI setting on.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says its language model could not be loaded or run. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: My language model could not be loaded. What would you like to do?
strings.de: Mein Sprachmodell konnte nicht geladen werden. Was möchtest du tun?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says the typed text was too long for the language model. The conversation about it is forgotten, so the next sentence works again.
strings.en: That was too long for me, so I forgot it. Please say it again, shorter.
strings.de: Das war zu lang für mich, darum habe ich es vergessen. Sag es bitte noch einmal, kürzer.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says the language model set up cannot answer this kind of question.
strings.en: The language model you set up cannot answer that kind of question.
strings.de: Das eingestellte Sprachmodell kann diese Art von Frage nicht beantworten.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says the answer of the language model could not be used.
strings.en: I could not use the answer of my language model. Please try again, maybe in other words.
strings.de: Die Antwort meines Sprachmodells war nicht brauchbar. Versuche es bitte noch einmal, vielleicht mit anderen Worten.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says the AI server does not answer or did not accept the request (wrong key, wrong model, no connection).
strings.en: The AI server does not answer or did not accept the request. Please check the connection and the AI settings.
strings.de: Der KI-Server antwortet nicht oder hat die Anfrage nicht angenommen. Prüfe bitte die Verbindung und die KI-Einstellungen.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says nothing was sent because the user has not agreed to send texts to the AI server yet.
strings.en: Nothing was sent: you have not agreed to send this kind of data to this AI server yet. You can do that in the AI settings.
strings.de: Es wurde nichts gesendet: Du hast dem Senden dieser Art von Daten an diesen KI-Server noch nicht zugestimmt. Das geht in den KI-Einstellungen.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says something broke inside the app while the language model was asked; the model itself is not to blame.
strings.en: Something went wrong inside the app. Please try again.
strings.de: In der App ist etwas schiefgegangen. Versuche es bitte noch einmal.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Line shown while the language model works on a typed sentence.
Hermes chat (F2): Line shown while the language model is loaded into memory before it can work on a typed sentence; this takes a few seconds.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks to confirm a tidy-up it understood from a sentence. {source} is the folder to tidy up, {target} the folder the files go to, each named the way the chat names folders: its name or a path starting with ~, {mode} is empty or one of the two phrases for copying or moving that start with a comma. The question ends with a question mark.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks to confirm a tidy-up it understood from a sentence when no target folder was named. {source} is the folder to tidy up, named the way the chat names folders: its name or a path starting with ~, {mode} is empty or one of the two phrases for copying or moving that start with a comma.
Hermes chat (F2): Added to the tidy-up confirmation when the user said the files shall be moved. Starts with a comma and a space.
Hermes chat (F2): Added to the tidy-up confirmation when the user said the files shall be copied. Starts with a comma and a space.
Hermes chat (F2): Primary button that confirms what Hermes understood. Nothing is moved by it; a trial run comes first.
Hermes chat (F2): Button under the tidy-up confirmation: choose another folder to file into.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks which folder the files shall go to instead. Folder buttons follow.
strings.en: Which folder shall they go to?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button label in the greeting for a folder where new documents arrive, e.g. Downloads. {folder} is the folder name.
Hermes chat (F2): button label in the greeting for a folder where the user keeps their documents (a target folder). {folder} is the folder name.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes does not know yet what a folder is for and asks whether it is a read folder (Hermes takes documents from it and sorts them) or a write folder (Hermes files documents into it). Two buttons follow. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: What is {folder} for: shall I read documents from it or write documents into it?
strings.de: Wofür ist {folder}: Soll ich von dort Dokumente lesen oder dorthin Dokumente schreiben?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button: the folder becomes a read folder, Hermes takes documents from it and sorts them (an inbox such as Downloads).
Hermes chat (F2): button: the folder becomes a write folder, Hermes files documents into it.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes found photos or scans in the folder it can only read with text recognition, and the text recognition models are not installed. {folder} is the folder name, {count} the number of images.
strings.en: {folder} holds {count} photos or scans I can't read without text recognition. Shall I read them too?
strings.de: In {folder} liegen {count} Fotos oder Scans, die ich ohne Texterkennung nicht lesen kann. Soll ich sie mitlesen?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button answering yes to reading photos and scans with text recognition.
Hermes chat (F2): button answering no to reading photos and scans.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes opened the download of the text recognition models and waits for it. A button follows to go on once the models are there.
strings.en: I opened the download of the text recognition models. Once they are there, press the button and I'll read the photos.
strings.de: Ich habe den Download der Texterkennung geöffnet. Sobald sie da ist, drück den Knopf, dann lese ich die Fotos mit.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button to go on reading the photos once the text recognition models are installed.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says it skips the photos and scans. {count} is the number of images.
strings.en: Fine, I'll leave the {count} photos and scans out.
strings.de: Gut, die {count} Fotos und Scans lasse ich aus.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button among the folders to file into; it opens the folder picker to choose or make a new folder to file into.
Hermes chat (F2): button among the folders to file into; Hermes then asks for every file where it goes.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes asks where one file goes; buttons with the folders follow. **Double asterisks** mark bold text. {name} is the file name, {position} the number of the file in the folder, {total} how many files there are.
Hermes chat (F2): button to leave one file where it is.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says that nothing is filed because the user left every file where it is.
strings.en: Then I'll leave everything where it is.
strings.de: Dann lasse ich alles, wo es ist.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): the folder to file into has no order yet; Hermes asks how to order what it puts there. Buttons follow. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: {folder} has no order yet. How should I order what I put there?
strings.de: {folder} hat noch keine Ordnung. Wie soll ich ordnen, was ich dort ablege?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): button: file by year, a folder for every year.
Hermes chat (F2): button: file by sender, a folder for every sender.
Hermes chat (F2): button: file by kind of document, a folder for every kind.
Hermes chat (F2): button: file everything into the one folder without subfolders.
Hermes chat (F2): Hermes found no folder for the word the user used in a change of order and asks which area of the filing is meant. A button for every area follows.

Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says what the answer Always does: it files the folder once in the Filing tab now, and after that files new files by itself when it is sure and shows the rest in that tab. Nothing is switched on before the run in the tab is filed. {folder} is the folder.
strings.en: Understood: I'll file {folder} once in the Filing tab now. After that I file new files myself when I'm sure, and show you the rest there.
strings.de: Verstanden: Ich sortiere {folder} jetzt einmal im Tab Ablegen ein. Danach lege ich neue Dateien selbst ab, wenn ich mir sicher bin; den Rest zeige ich dir dort.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes says what the answer Always does while the user decides file by file in the chat: it watches the folder, files at once what a confirmed rule of the user matches, and leaves everything else waiting for the user's OK. {folder} is the watched folder.
strings.en: Understood: I'm watching {folder}. What one of your rules matches I file; everything else waits for your OK.
strings.de: Verstanden: ich beobachte {folder}. Was eine deiner Regeln trifft, lege ich ab; alles andere wartet auf dein OK.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Hermes answers a greeting, thanks or the question what it can do, with one line on what it does. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: I'm Hermes: I tidy up your documents, find them and change how your documents are ordered. What would you like to do?
strings.de: Ich bin Hermes: Ich räume deine Dokumente auf, finde sie und ändere, wie deine Dokumente geordnet sind. Was möchtest du tun?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): the user said nothing should be changed; Hermes agrees politely. Buttons with things it can do follow.
strings.en: Alright, I'll leave everything as it is.
strings.de: In Ordnung, ich lasse alles so, wie es ist.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): one line under the card of the areas Hermes read in a folder, shown while the AI has not yet understood every document with a text. {done} is how many it understood, {total} how many documents have a text. The rest continues in the background.
strings.en: {done} of {total} documents understood, the rest continues in the background.
strings.de: {done} von {total} Dokumenten verstanden, der Rest läuft im Hintergrund.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): the user wrote something Hermes took for small talk or could not use right after a request, so it was probably about that request. Hermes asks again; buttons with the areas it knows follow. The example in quotes is what the user could type.
strings.en: Is that about what we just did? Please tell me again with the area, for example “only Bank by year”.
strings.de: Meinst du das zur letzten Frage? Sag es mir bitte noch einmal mit dem Bereich, zum Beispiel „nur Bank nach Jahr“.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): The number of files next to the name of an area in the list of areas. {count} is a number greater than one.
Hermes chat (F2): The number of files next to the name of an area in the list of areas when there is exactly one file.
Hermes chat (F2): The short word before the example path under an area in the list of areas, as in 'e.g. 2024/Bank/statement.pdf'.
Hermes chat (F2): Joins the names of a folder level that has several fixed choices, as in 'Account, Loan or Messages'. {list} is a comma separated list, {last} the final name.

Hermes chat (F2): Row under the areas of a folder when more areas exist than are listed and all of them are named. The number of files in them is added after the row. {names} is a comma separated list, {count} a number.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button after a folder could not be read (read the same folder again) or after Hermes could not start (start it again).
Hermes chat (F2): Short second line under the question whether to copy or move the files: what each choice does with the originals. {folder} is the name of the folder the files come from.
strings.en: Copy leaves the originals in “{folder}”, move clears them out of there.
strings.de: Kopieren lässt die Originale in „{folder}“ liegen, Verschieben räumt sie dort weg.

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): One message at the end of a trial run that files nothing, when some of the files are in the filing folder already. {total} is the number of files looked at, {dupes} how many are there already, {rest} the others, {ai_note} is empty or the sentence about how far the AI is. Buttons with what to do follow.
strings.en: Of {total} files, {dupes} are already in the target folder. For the other {rest} I don't know yet where they belong{ai_note}. What shall I do?
strings.de: Von {total} Dateien sind {dupes} schon im Schreib-Ordner. Für die anderen {rest} weiß ich noch nicht, wohin sie gehören{ai_note}. Was soll ich tun?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): One message at the end of a trial run that files nothing, when none of the files is in the filing folder yet. {rest} is the number of files, {ai_note} is empty or the sentence about how far the AI is. Buttons with what to do follow.
strings.en: For {rest} files I don't know yet where they belong{ai_note}. What shall I do?
strings.de: Für {rest} Dateien weiß ich noch nicht, wohin sie gehören{ai_note}. Was soll ich tun?

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Added to the message that the app does not know yet where files belong, while the AI has not read every document yet. {done} is how many documents it understood, {all} how many have a text. It begins with a colon.
strings.en: : I am only just reading your folder, {done} of {all} documents are understood
strings.de: : Ich lese deinen Ordner gerade erst ein, {done} von {all} Dokumenten sind verstanden

strings.context: Hermes chat (F2): Answer button at the end of a trial run that files nothing: stop for now and come back later; nothing is remembered.
Hermes chat (F2): Answer button at the end of a trial run: move the files that are in the filing folder already to the trash. {count} is their number.
Heading over the first run of pages in the feature list of the settings tab: look, language, keys. One word.
Heading over the second run of pages in the feature list of the settings tab: programs that open files, and servers. One word, noun, plural.
Heading over the third run of pages in the feature list of the settings tab: the Index, read errors and reports. One word, noun, plural.
Heading over the last run of pages in the feature list of the settings tab: the Hermes sorting, its rules and tags. Hermes is the name of the AI sorting module, a Beta mark follows it. Keep the name.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab and title of its page: what ncrs knows about the user's files (text, sender, kind, date). One word, noun.
Sentence under the title of the Index page of the settings tab. The index is the database in which ncrs keeps what it read from the files. The Hermes overview says whether it is encrypted.
strings.en: What ncrs knows about your files: text, sender, kind, date. Stored on this computer; the Hermes overview says whether it is encrypted.
strings.de: Was ncrs über deine Dateien weiß: Text, Absender, Art, Datum. Liegt auf diesem Computer; die Hermes-Übersicht zeigt, ob er verschlüsselt ist.

strings.context: Dim word beside the entry Hermes in the feature list of the settings tab and beside the title of its page: what Hermes does. Verb as noun, one word.
Heading of the section of the Index page of the settings tab that lists the folders the index reads.
Heading of the section of the Index page of the settings tab about reading text from scans and photos (OCR).

Entry of the feature list on the settings tab and title of its page: the AI model Hermes (the module that sorts documents) uses, and the switch that turns Hermes on. German KI is short for künstliche Intelligenz. Short.
Sentence under the title of the AI page of the settings tab. Hermes is the module that sorts documents; the chat is opened with F2.
strings.en: One model for everything: sorting, chat (F2), rules, name suggestions.
strings.de: Ein Modell für alles: Sortieren, Chat (F2), Regeln, Namensvorschläge.

strings.context: Heading of the section of the AI page of the settings tab about the AI model: where it runs and how it is set up.
Label of the row of the AI page about the AI model on this computer; its state and the button to load it follow. The word model is meant to be searchable.
Label of the row of the AI page with the buttons that test the own AI server and save its address, model and key. Its status line tells what the test found.
Heading of the section of the Index page of the settings tab in which the user enters their own names, accounts and tax numbers.
Heading of the section of the Index page of the settings tab about the encryption of the index. One word, noun.
Heading of the section of the Index page of the settings tab that shows how far the index is: counts, pause, load, unreadable files. One word, noun.
Label of the row of the Index page that chooses which folders the index reads. Noun, plural.
Option of the segment in the Folders row of the Index page: read everything on the computer. Not available yet; the option is dimmed.
Option of the segment in the Folders row of the Index page: read only the folders listed below.
Dim sentence under the title of the Folders row of the Index page: only the folders listed below are read; the option Everything (the whole computer) is dimmed and comes in a later version.
strings.en: Only the folders below are read. Reading the whole computer comes in a later version.
strings.de: Gelesen werden nur die Ordner unten. Den ganzen Computer lesen kommt in einer späteren Version.

strings.context: Warning under a folder line on the Index and Hermes pages: the folder is on a drive that is not connected right now.
Button under the folder list of the Index and Hermes pages: opens the system folder dialog to add a folder. The plus sign belongs to the label.
Line on the Index page when no folder is listed.
strings.en: No folder yet. The index only reads folders you add.
strings.de: Noch kein Ordner. Der Index liest nur Ordner, die du hinzufügst.

strings.context: Label of the row of the Index page about reading scans and photos with the recognizer the operating system brings (macOS Vision). Only shown on macOS.
Description under the row about reading scans and photos on the Index page. macOS Vision is the name of Apple's recognizer.
State shown at the right of a row of the Index page: the function is ready to use. One word.
Label of the row of the Index page about the second text recognizer that ncrs downloads.
Description under the row about the fallback recognizer on the Index page. It consists of 2 files of 40 MB together.
strings.en: Steps in when macOS cannot read a page. 2 files, 40 MB. The only recognizer on Linux and Windows.
strings.de: Springt ein, wenn macOS eine Seite nicht lesen kann. 2 Dateien, 40 MB. Auf Linux und Windows der einzige Erkenner.

strings.context: Second line under the AI model row of the Index page of the settings tab when the model is in memory. Takes the file name, the memory it uses with its unit (for example 2.5 GB) and what it computes on: the name of the graphics device, or the word for the processor.
Part of the second line under the AI model row of the Index page: the model computes on the processor, not on a graphics card. Follows the words 'runs on'.
Second line under the AI model row of the Index page when the model file could not be used. Takes the reason, which is English and stays untranslated.
Description under the row about the AI model on this computer on the AI page. Qwen3.5-4B is the name of the model.
strings.en: Qwen3.5-4B. Without a model only file names and dates.
strings.de: Qwen3.5-4B. Ohne Modell nur Dateinamen und Datum.

strings.context: State of the AI model on the AI page while the Hermes switch there is off. Short phrase; Hermes is the name of the filing assistant.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is not on this computer.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is being downloaded right now.
State of the AI model on the Index page: the model is on this computer and ready. One word.
State of the AI on the Index page: an own server is used instead of the local model. {model} is the model name on that server.
State of the AI on the Index page: it could not start. The reason is on the status page.
State of the AI on the Index page: it was switched on and starts when ncrs is started the next time.
Description under the rows of own names, accounts and tax numbers on the Index page. The typed text is added with the plus button or Enter.
strings.en: Several allowed: separate them with commas or semicolons.
strings.de: Mehrere möglich: mit Komma oder Semikolon trennen.

strings.context: Button next to the field of an own detail (name, account, tax number) on the Index page: adds what is typed. A plus sign.
Row on the Index page. {documents} is how many documents the index holds, {understood} how many of them the AI has read and sorted.
Description under the row with the document counts on the Index page.
strings.en: The rest runs in the background.

strings.context: Button on the Index page that pauses the background work of the index. Verb.
Button on the Index page that continues the paused background work of the index. Verb.
Label of the row of the Index page that chooses how much of the computer the index may use. Noun.
Description under the Load row on the Index page.
strings.en: How much of your computer the index may use.
strings.de: Wie viel Rechner der Index nehmen darf.

strings.context: Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use little, so the computer stays usable.
Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use a moderate share.
Option of the Load segment on the Index page: use all the computer can give.
Row on the Index page. {count} is how many files could not be read; at least 2.
Row on the Index page when exactly one file could not be read.
Button in the row of unreadable files on the Index page: opens the list of the files and why they could not be read. Verb.

Description under the Hermes switch at the top of the AI page of the settings tab. Off: Hermes watches no read folders and asks no AI model for sorting documents, the chat, rename suggestions or learning rules.
strings.en: Off: no folders watched, no model asked.
strings.de: Aus: keine Ordner beobachtet, kein Modell gefragt.

strings.context: Option of the segment at the top of the AI page: Hermes works. One word.
Option of the segment at the top of the AI page: Hermes watches no folders and calls no AI model. One word.
Heading of the section of the Hermes page that lists the folders Hermes picks up new documents from. Compound noun: read folders.
Sentence under the heading Read folders on the Hermes page.
strings.en: Where new documents arrive. Each line says what Hermes does with them.
strings.de: Wo neue Dokumente ankommen. Jede Zeile sagt, was Hermes damit macht.

strings.context: Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: Hermes reads the folder all the time. Lower case, one or two words.
Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: Hermes reads the folder only when the user asks in the chat. Lower case.
Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: files are moved out of the folder when filed. Lower case verb.
Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: files are copied and the originals stay in the folder. Lower case verb.
Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: Hermes files new files of the folder by itself when it is sure. Lower case, one word.
Button in the row of a read folder on the Hermes page that Hermes files continuously: Hermes stops filing its new files by itself; the folder stays a read folder.
Part of the status text of a read folder on the Hermes page: images are read as well. Lower case.
Button on a read folder line of the Hermes page: opens the small dialog that changes what Hermes does with the folder. Verb.
Button under the read folder list of the Hermes page: opens the Hermes chat (F2), which sets the folders up in conversation.
Line on the Hermes page when no read folder is listed.
Title of the small dialog opened with Change on a read folder of the Hermes page. Compound noun: read folder.
Question in the read folder dialog: whether Hermes reads the folder all the time or only when asked.
strings.en: When does Hermes read this folder?

strings.context: Option in the read folder dialog: Hermes reads the folder all the time.
Option in the read folder dialog: Hermes reads the folder only when the user asks in the chat.
Checkbox in the read folder dialog: images are read as well.
Heading of the section of the Hermes page that shows the order Hermes learned from the user's files. Noun.
Sentence under the heading Order on the Hermes page. Nothing can be entered there; changes go through the chat.
strings.en: What Hermes has learned from your files. It files new documents the same way. Nothing to enter here; change it in the chat.
strings.de: Was Hermes aus deinen Dateien gelernt hat. Neue Dokumente legt er genauso ab. Nichts einzutragen; ändern geht im Chat.

strings.context: Line under the Order heading on the Hermes page when Hermes has learned nothing yet.
strings.en: Nothing learned yet. Let Hermes read a folder in the chat.
strings.de: Noch nichts gelernt. Lass Hermes im Chat einen Ordner lesen.

strings.context: Line under the Order heading on the Hermes page while the folders are being looked at.
Name line of an area in the Order section of the Hermes page. An area is a part of the filing structure, for example Bank. {name} is its name, {count} the number of files; at least 2.
Name line of an area in the Order section of the Hermes page when it holds exactly one file. {name} is the name of the area.
Button on an area line of the Hermes page: opens the Hermes chat (F2) at the change of this area.
Line under the first three areas of the Order section. {count} is the number of areas not shown; at least 2.
Line under the first three areas of the Order section when one more area is not shown.
Button in the Order section of the Hermes page: shows all areas.
Button in the Order section of the Hermes page after all areas are shown: shows only the first three again.
Heading of the section of the Hermes page that lists what Hermes filed recently. Noun.
Heading of the section of the Hermes page about the saved chats with Hermes. Plural noun.
Row of the Hermes page: after how long old chats of the Hermes chat are deleted, counted from the last time a chat was used. The choices are at the right.
Note under the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: when it happens.
strings.en: Old chats are deleted when ncrs starts.
strings.de: Alte Chats werden beim Start von ncrs gelöscht.

strings.context: Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats are never deleted by age. One word.
Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats unused for 30 days are deleted.
Choice of the row about deleting old chats on the Hermes page: chats unused for 90 days are deleted.
Line under the History heading on the Hermes page when Hermes has not filed anything yet.
Line of the last run in the History section. {when} is a date and time such as Today 14:02, {count} the number of files (at least 2), {from} the folder they came from.
Line of the last run in the History section when it filed exactly one file. {when} is a date and time, {from} the folder the file came from.
Button on the run in the History section: puts the files of the run back. Verb phrase.
Notice when the last run could not be put back. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The last run could not be undone: {reason}
strings.de: Der letzte Lauf konnte nicht rückgängig gemacht werden: {reason}

strings.context: Reason inside the notice that the last run could not be undone, when the index answered something other than the undo result. Short clause, no full stop.
strings.en: the index gave an unexpected answer

strings.context: Notice after a run was put back but some files stayed where Hermes had put them, because they changed or their old place is taken. {left} is a number.
strings.en: Run undone, but {left} files stayed where they are: they changed or their old place is taken.
strings.de: Lauf rückgängig gemacht, aber {left} Dateien sind geblieben: Sie haben sich geändert oder ihr alter Platz ist belegt.

strings.context: Notice on the Index page when the numbers of the index could not be read, so the page shows nothing instead of the real figures. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The index could not be read: {reason}
strings.de: Der Index konnte nicht gelesen werden: {reason}

strings.context: Reason inside the notices that the index could not be read or the last run could not be undone, when the work in the background ended without an answer. Short clause, no full stop.
strings.en: the work in the background stopped unexpectedly
strings.de: die Arbeit im Hintergrund ist unerwartet abgebrochen

strings.context: Title of the question before a downloaded model is deleted from this computer.
Question before the fallback text recognizer is deleted from this computer.
strings.en: Remove the fallback recognizer from this Mac? You can load it again later.
strings.de: Den Ersatz-Erkenner von diesem Mac entfernen? Du kannst ihn später wieder laden.

strings.context: Question before the AI model is deleted from this computer.
strings.en: Remove the AI model from this Mac? You can load it again later.
strings.de: Das KI-Modell von diesem Mac entfernen? Du kannst es später wieder laden.

strings.context: Notice when a model could not be deleted. {reason} is the system's explanation.
strings.en: The model could not be removed: {reason}
strings.de: Das Modell konnte nicht entfernt werden: {reason}

strings.context: Description under a folder of the Index page. {path} is where the folder is, {count} how many documents the index holds from it; at least 2.
Description under a folder of the Index page when the index holds exactly one document from it. {path} is where the folder is.
Label of the row of the Index page that shows whether the index is encrypted. Noun.
Question in the read folder dialog: whether the files are copied out of the folder or moved when filed.
Option in the read folder dialog: files are copied and the originals stay in the folder. Verb.
Option in the read folder dialog: files are moved out of the folder when filed. Verb.
Day word in a run line of the History section on the Hermes page, followed by the time: Today 14:02.
Day word in a run line of the History section on the Hermes page, followed by the time: Yesterday 09:30.
Run line of the History section when the folder the files went to is known. {line} is the line up to the source folder, for example: Today 14:02 · 12 files from Downloads. {to} is the target folder.
Description under a run of the History section: some of the folders the files went to. {folders} is a comma separated list of paths.
Button under the last runs of the History section on the Hermes page: lists all runs that are kept.
Button in the row of a rule or a report on the settings pages Rules and Reports: opens the small dialog to change it.
Button under the list on the Rules page of the settings: opens the dialog for a new rule. The plus sign belongs to the label.
Title of the dialog in which an existing rule is changed on the Rules page of the settings.
Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: how the Monitor page measures and shows the machine.
Line under the heading of the Monitor page on the settings tab. The Monitor page lists CPU, memory, drives, network and running tasks.
strings.en: What the Monitor page measures, how often, and what the status bar shows of it.
strings.de: Was die Seite Monitor misst, wie oft, und was die Statusleiste davon zeigt.

strings.context: Entry of the feature list on the settings tab: the page about the installed version of ncrs, the check for a newer one and how to install it.
Line under the heading of the Updates page on the settings tab. The page shows the installed version, the switch of the daily check and, when a newer version exists, how to get it.
strings.en: The installed version, whether ncrs looks for a newer one, and how to install it.
strings.de: Die installierte Version, ob ncrs nach einer neueren sucht, und wie man sie installiert.

strings.context: Label of the row that sets how often the Monitor page measures the machine, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets how the tasks on the Monitor page are sorted at first, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets the unit of the network speed on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether the drive list on the Monitor page shows used or free space, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the CPU load in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the memory use in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the swap use in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the load average in the status bar, on the settings tab. Not offered on Windows.
Label of the on/off switch that puts the network speed in the status bar, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether the status bar shows numbers or symbols for the chosen values, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether network interfaces without traffic are listed on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Label of the row that sets whether system volumes are listed among the drives on the Monitor page, on the settings tab.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every second.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every two seconds.
Choice of the refresh row on the settings tab: measure every five seconds.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by processor use.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by memory use.
Choice of the task sort row on the settings tab: by the processor time a task has used.
Choice of the network speed row on the settings tab: speed in bytes per second.
Choice of the network speed row on the settings tab: speed in bits per second.
Choice of the drive column row on the settings tab: show the used space.
Choice of the drive column row on the settings tab: show the free space.
Choice of the status bar style row on the settings tab: percentages and speeds as numbers.
Choice of the status bar style row on the settings tab: a small bar symbol instead of a number.
Choice of a visibility row on the Monitor page settings: do not list these entries.
Choice of a visibility row on the Monitor page settings: list these entries.

Entry of the command palette that runs the key action system_monitor, which opens the Monitor page with the load of the computer. The plain name of what the action does, as short as a menu entry; the key bound to it is shown beside it.
Name of the Monitor page: the mode field in its status bar and the tab in the title bar.
The mode field at the left end of the status bar of the Monitor page, in capitals like the one of the settings tab. The same word as the page's name.
Shown on the Monitor page until the first measurement of the computer has arrived.
Header of the Monitor page: how long the computer has been running. {time} is a duration such as 3d 4h.
Title of the processor meter at the top of the Monitor page.
Title of the main memory meter at the top of the Monitor page.
Title of the swap meter at the top of the Monitor page; swap is memory spilled to disk.
Title of the load average meter on the Monitor page. Not shown on Windows.
Line under the processor meter. {brand} is the processor model, {cores} the number of cores.
Line under the memory meter. Placeholders are sizes such as 8.2G.
Line under the swap meter. Placeholders are sizes such as 1.5G.
Line under the load meter: the load average over one, five and fifteen minutes.
Heading of the network block on the Monitor page, which lists the network interfaces.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: the name of the interface.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: data received per second.
Column title in the network block of the Monitor page: data sent per second.
Heading of the drives block on the Monitor page, which lists mounted volumes.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: space in use.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: space still free.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: size of the volume.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: data read per second.
Column title in the drives block of the Monitor page: data written per second.
Heading of the block on the Monitor page that lists temperature sensors.
Heading of the task list on the Monitor page, which lists running programs.
Line next to the task list heading. {running}, {sleeping} and {other} are counts; {sort} is the name of the column the list is sorted by.
Hint in the empty filter field above the task list on the Monitor page. {key} is the shortcut that focuses it.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: share of processor time in percent.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: share of main memory in percent.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: resident memory in bytes.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the process number.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the owner of the task.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: processor time the task has used.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: one letter for running or sleeping.
Column title of the task list on the Monitor page: the command line of the task.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: ends the task after a confirmation.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: copies its command line to the clipboard.
Context menu entry of a task on the Monitor page: shows the folder of its program in the active panel.
Title of the confirmation dialog for ending a task on the Monitor page.
Line in the kill dialog naming the task. {name} is the program, {pid} its process number.
Warning in the kill dialog: the task ends at once and unsaved work in it is lost.
strings.en: The task ends at once. Unsaved work in it is lost.
strings.de: Der Prozess wird sofort beendet. Nicht gespeicherte Arbeit darin geht verloren.

strings.context: Button of the kill dialog that ends the task.
Hint in the middle of the status bar of the Monitor page while every process has its own row. g is the key; it groups the processes by program.
Hint in the middle of the status bar of the Monitor page while processes of one program are shown as one row. g is the key; it shows every process again.
Right side of the status bar of the Monitor page: how often it measures. {seconds} is a number.
Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the task is ncrs itself and is not ended. {name} is the program.
strings.en: {name} is ncrs itself and cannot be killed
strings.de: {name} ist ncrs selbst und kann nicht beendet werden

strings.context: Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the task has ended or the number belongs to another task now. {name} is the program.
strings.en: {name} is gone or has changed, nothing was killed
strings.de: {name} ist beendet oder ein anderer Prozess, nichts wurde beendet

strings.context: Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the system did not let the task end. {name} is the program.
Error in the status bar of the Monitor page: the measurement failed. {reason} is the system's message.
Notice in the status bar of the Monitor page after a task ended. {name} is the program.
Tooltip of the CPU and memory text at the right end of the status bar; a click opens the Monitor page.
Notice in the status bar after the command line of a task from the Monitor page was copied to the clipboard.

Entry of the command palette and the File menu that runs the key action open_terminal: starts the user's terminal in the folder of the active panel, or in the folder under the cursor. Imperative, as short as a menu entry; the key bound to it is shown beside it.
Entry of the context menu: starts the user's terminal in the folder under the cursor, or in the folder of the panel when the cursor is on a file. Verb, imperative.

Status bar notice when 'Open terminal here' is used while the active panel shows a server, the inside of an archive or a list of search hits: there is no folder on this computer to start a terminal in.
strings.en: A terminal needs a folder on this computer
strings.de: Ein Terminal braucht einen Ordner auf diesem Computer

strings.context: Status bar error when 'Open terminal here' finds no terminal on the computer and none is set in the settings.
strings.en: No terminal found. Choose one under Settings > Programs.
strings.de: Kein Terminal gefunden. Wähle eines unter Einstellungen > Programme.

strings.context: Status bar error when the terminal could not be started. Takes the folder name and the OS reason.
strings.en: Could not open a terminal in {name}: {reason}
strings.de: Terminal in {name} konnte nicht geöffnet werden: {reason}

strings.context: Error in the connect dialog when the server ended the connection setup without showing a host key, so it cannot be checked. Takes the host.
strings.en: {host} did not show a host key, so the server cannot be checked
strings.de: {host} hat keinen Hostschlüssel gezeigt, der Server lässt sich daher nicht prüfen

strings.context: Reason shown inside the failure text of the connect dialog when the user trusts a new host key but ncrs has no file to keep it in (no home folder known). Short, without a full stop.
strings.en: there is no file to keep the host key in
strings.de: es gibt keine Datei, in der der Hostschlüssel gespeichert werden kann

strings.context: Name of a setting on the programs page: the terminal that 'Open terminal here' starts. One word, noun.
Explanation under the terminal setting: Automatic means the first terminal found on the computer; in an own command, {path} is replaced by the folder.
strings.en: Automatic takes the first terminal found. In your own command {path} stands for the folder.
strings.de: Automatisch nimmt das erste gefundene Terminal. Im eigenen Befehl steht {path} für den Ordner.

strings.context: Name of an on/off switch on the programs page, Windows only: ncrs is added to the right-click menu of folders and files in the Explorer.
strings.en: Show in the Explorer context menu

strings.context: Explanation under the Explorer context menu switch on the programs page (Windows only).
strings.en: Adds "Open in ncrs" to the right-click menu of folders, of the folder background and of files.
strings.de: Fügt „In ncrs öffnen“ zum Rechtsklick-Menü von Ordnern, Ordnerhintergrund und Dateien hinzu.

strings.context: Name of an on/off switch on the programs page (Windows and Linux only): ncrs is the program that opens folders when another program or the system asks for the folder manager.
strings.en: ncrs as the default file manager

strings.context: Explanation under the default file manager switch on the programs page. Turning it off gives folders back to the program that opened them before.
strings.en: Folders other programs open go to ncrs. Turning this off goes back to the earlier choice.
strings.de: Ordner, die andere Programme öffnen, gehen an ncrs. Beim Ausschalten gilt wieder die frühere Wahl.

strings.context: Dim info line at the end of the programs page on macOS, where the switches of the other systems do not exist. Says where ncrs shows up as a program for folders and files. 'Open With' is the Finder menu entry, use the system's own name for it.
strings.en: On macOS, ncrs is listed in the Finder under “Open With” for folders and files.
strings.de: Auf macOS steht ncrs im Finder unter „Öffnen mit“ für Ordner und Dateien.

strings.context: Status message when the default file manager or Explorer menu switch on the programs page could not be changed. {reason} is the system's own error text.
The words of the ncrs entry in the Windows Explorer right-click menu. Starts with a verb; written into the registry when the switch is turned on.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page: the first terminal found on the computer is used. Takes the name of that terminal.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page when no terminal was found on the computer: the same 'Automatic' choice, without a name.
Choice in the terminal list on the programs page: the user types the program and its arguments themselves.
Placeholder in the empty field of the own terminal command on the programs page. An example line; {path} must stay as it is.
Chat reply when a filing folder is opened that holds several areas. {count} is the number of subfolders; buttons with their names follow.
strings.en: {count} areas lie here. Which one shall I open?
strings.de: Hier liegen {count} Bereiche. Welchen soll ich öffnen?

strings.context: Chat reply when a filing folder is opened that holds exactly one area. A button with its name follows.
strings.en: One area lies here. Shall I open it?
strings.de: Hier liegt ein Bereich. Soll ich ihn öffnen?

strings.context: Chat reply when an opened filing folder holds no files. {folder} is its name. Followed by a suggested order and buttons.
strings.en: {folder} is empty. Should something go in?
strings.de: {folder} ist leer. Soll da was rein?

strings.context: Title of the card that lists the folder levels and file name Hermes found in a filing folder. {count} is the number of levels.
Title of the card that lists the folder levels after the user started to change them. Replaces the title of the levels found.
Title of the card with the standard order proposed for a new, empty filing folder. {count} is the number of levels.
Last line of the levels card. {fitting} files follow the found order, {total} files were checked.
Chat text under the levels card when the order the model recognised fits too few of the files. {fitting} of {total} files follow it. The only button left is the one that changes the levels.
strings.en: This order fits only {fitting} of {total} files, so I will not create a rule from it as it is. Change the levels.
strings.de: Diese Reihenfolge passt nur auf {fitting} von {total} Dateien, deshalb lege ich daraus nicht einfach eine Regel an. Ändere die Ebenen.

strings.context: One line below the levels card for a file that does not follow the found order. {file} is its path, {written} is the path the order would give it.
One line below the levels card for a file the found order cannot write a path for. {file} is its path.
strings.en: {file} cannot be written by this order
strings.de: {file} lässt sich mit dieser Ordnung nicht schreiben

strings.context: Button under the levels Hermes found: the levels are right, make the rule from them.
Button: set up the levels shown for an empty folder.
Button: change the levels shown.
Button: use the standard order year, then date_sender_kind as file name.
Button under the levels card after the user changed a level in words: take the levels as they now stand and go on to the trial of the rule.
Button under the levels card after a change: say one more change of the levels in words.
Button under the levels card after a change: throw the changes away and show the levels Hermes found again.
Button while the user changes the levels: nothing more to change, take the levels as they stand and go on to the trial of the rule. Always there, also before the first change.
Small line under a changed level in the levels card. {value} is what the level wrote before the change, from a real file.
Line under the levels card after a change when no existing file would be renamed or moved by the changed levels.
strings.en: On applying, no existing file changes.
strings.de: Beim Übernehmen ändert sich keine vorhandene Datei.

strings.context: Chat reply when the user names only a level number while changing the levels; asks what should be different on that level. {level} is the number as on the card.
strings.en: What should be different about level {level}?
strings.de: Was soll an Ebene {level} anders sein?

strings.context: Chat reply while changing the levels when the rule finds no document because the index has not read the folder's files yet. {known} of {total} files of {folder} are in the index; the levels stay as they are.
strings.en: The index knows only {known} of the {total} files in {folder} so far, Hermes is still reading the rest. The levels stay as they are: change them further, or say you are done and I will try again.
strings.de: Der Index kennt von den {total} Dateien in {folder} erst {known}, den Rest liest Hermes noch. Die Ebenen bleiben, wie sie sind: Ändere sie weiter, oder sag Bescheid, dass du fertig bist, dann versuche ich es noch einmal.

strings.context: Chat reply while changing the levels when the rule matches none of the files of the folder although the index knows them. {folder} is the folder name; the levels stay as they are.
strings.en: The rule for these levels matches none of the files in {folder}. The levels stay as they are: change them further, or say you are done and I will try again.
strings.de: Die Regel für diese Ebenen passt auf keine Datei in {folder}. Die Ebenen bleiben, wie sie sind: Ändere sie weiter, oder sag Bescheid, dass du fertig bist, dann versuche ich es noch einmal.

strings.context: Explains how to change the levels: tell it in a typed sentence; the buttons below finish. Examples with level numbers as on the card.
strings.en: Tell me in words what to change, for example "year and month together in level 2" or "date first in level 3". Say when you are done.
strings.de: Sag in Worten, was sich ändern soll, zum Beispiel „Jahr und Monat zusammen in Ebene 2“ oder „Datum vorne bei Ebene 3“. Sag Bescheid, wenn du fertig bist.

strings.context: Role of a folder level whose name is the same for all files: it stays as it is.
Role of the last level, the file name. {parts} are the fields it is made of.
Name of the day field in the levels card, one word.
Name of the recipient field in the levels card, one word.
Role of the file name when Hermes makes it automatically.
Question for the condition of the rule, after the levels are settled or when the user wants to change the condition. {folder} is the folder name.
strings.en: Which documents should the rule for {folder} apply to? For example "only from one sender" or "only if the text says invoice".
strings.de: Für welche Dokumente soll die Regel für {folder} gelten? Zum Beispiel „nur von einem Absender“ oder „nur wenn im Text Rechnung steht“.

strings.context: Button text that describes a rule: documents of one kind. {kind} is the kind.
Button text that describes a rule: documents of one sender. {sender} is the sender.
Button text that describes a rule: documents of one kind from one sender.
Chat reply when a proposed rule would file none of the documents the index knows.
strings.en: No document I know would go there. Describe it another way?
strings.de: Kein Dokument, das ich kenne, würde dorthin gehen. Beschreibst du es anders?

strings.context: Joins the conditions of a rule: all must hold. {list} is the list of conditions.
Joins the conditions of a rule: one must hold. {list} is the list of conditions.
Where the rule trial puts a document the rule does not settle: it waits in the review list.
Title of the card with the proposed rule in the chat.
Label in the proposal card, left of the condition of the rule in words: which documents the rule applies to.
Label in the proposal card, left of the folder levels in words: where the rule files the documents.
Label in the proposal card, left of the file name in words (for example date, sender).
Label in the proposal card, left of how many known documents the rule matches.
Value in the proposal card: how many documents the rule matches. {count} is a count.
Header of the list of example files in the proposal card; each shows where a document would go and, dim below it, where it lies now.
Header of the list in the changed-levels card of the files the changed levels would rename or move when applied. {count} is how many.
Last line under the example lines of the rule trial when more documents would move than are shown. {count} is how many are not shown.

Line of the rule trial about where the matching documents lie. {right} already lie in the archive where the rule would put them, {moves} would be renamed or moved (existing archive files included), {inbox} of those come from the source folders. All three are counts.
strings.en: Already filed correctly: {right} · Will be renamed or moved: {moves} ({inbox} of them from the read folders)
strings.de: Schon richtig abgelegt: {right} · Wird umbenannt oder verschoben: {moves} (davon {inbox} aus den Lesen-Ordnern)

strings.context: Button: store the proposed rule.
Chat reply after a rule was stored. {name} is the name of the rule, made from the fixed folder names of its filing, e.g. Work / Salary.
strings.en: Rule “{name}” saved. It applies from now on to new documents in the read folders.
strings.de: Regel „{name}“ gespeichert. Sie gilt ab jetzt für neue Dokumente in den Lesen-Ordnern.

strings.context: Chat reply after a rule that already existed was changed in place instead of adding a second one. {name} is the name of the rule, made from the fixed folder names of its filing, e.g. Work / Salary.
strings.en: Rule “{name}” changed. It applies from now on to new documents in the read folders.
strings.de: Regel „{name}“ angepasst. Sie gilt ab jetzt für neue Dokumente in den Lesen-Ordnern.

strings.context: Note under the levels card of an opened folder that an existing rule already files into. {folder} is the folder name, {name} the name of the rule. Creating the rule from the levels changes that rule instead of adding a second one.
strings.en: {folder} already has the rule “{name}”. Creating the rule changes it.
strings.de: Für {folder} gibt es schon die Regel „{name}“. Wenn du die Regel anlegst, wird sie angepasst.

strings.context: Sentence before the question after a rule was stored, when files that already lie in the archive would be renamed or moved too. {count} is the number of those files, {folder} the name of the archive folder they lie in.
strings.en: {count} files in {folder} would be renamed or moved.
strings.de: {count} Dateien in {folder} würden umbenannt oder verschoben.

strings.context: Added to the sentence about archive files that would be renamed or moved: some files cannot be handled in this run because another file wants the same name or two files would swap names. They stay where they are. {count} is the number of those files.
strings.en: {count} more cannot be renamed now because their new name is taken or they would swap places; they stay.
strings.de: {count} weitere lassen sich jetzt nicht umbenennen, weil der neue Name vergeben ist oder sie die Plätze tauschen würden; sie bleiben liegen.
